test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 25 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A diver rowing at the speed of 3 km/h in still water takes double the time going 50 km upstream compared to going 50 km downstream. The speed of the diver downstream is:
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of diver in still water (u) = 3 km/h

Distance upstream = Distance downstream = 50 km

Time upstream is double the time downstream.

**Formula used:**

Speed downstream = u + v

Speed upstream = u - v

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the stream be v km/h.

Time upstream = 2 × Time downstream

⇒ 50 ÷ (u - v) = 2 × (50 ÷ (u + v))

⇒ 50 ÷ (3 - v) = 2 × (50 ÷ (3 + v))

⇒ 1 ÷ (3 - v) = 2 ÷ (3 + v)

⇒ 3 + v = 2 × (3 - v)

⇒ 3 + v = 6 - 2v

⇒ 3v = 3

⇒ v = 1 km/h

Speed downstream = u + v = 3 + 1 = 4 km/h

**∴ The speed of the diver downstream is 4 km/h.**
